item.title: Smoke Alert FOR MUNDARING, SAWYERS VALLEY, PARKERVILLE AND SURROUNDING AREAS IN THE SHIRE OF MUNDARING
item.description:
The following alert has been issued by the Parks and Wildlife Service at the Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions.

This is a new alert.

Time of issue: 10:14 AM

Date of issue: 06 Nov 2026

Smoke Alert for MUNDARING, SAWYERS VALLEY, PARKERVILLE and surrounding areas in the SHIRE OF MUNDARING

  • A Smoke Alert has been issued for people in MUNDARING, SAWYERS VALLEY, PARKERVILLE and surrounding areas in the SHIRE OF MUNDARING.

  • The smoke is the result of a Parks and Wildlife Service prescribed burn being carried out south-east of Mundaring.

  • Smoke may settle in low lying areas before clearing Saturday morning.

WHAT TO DO

  • Shut doors and windows and turn off air-conditioners.
  • If driving through the area, turn on headlights and drive slowly. If you cannot see clearly, pull over to the left, keep your headlights and hazard lights on, and wait until the smoke clears.
  • People with asthma and pre-existing respiratory or cardiovascular illnesses should follow their pre-prepared treatment plan.
  • If affected by smoke contact your doctor or call 1800MEDICARE (1800 633 422).
  • Watch for emergency services personnel and follow their directions.

ROAD CLOSURES AND CONDITIONS

Motorists are asked to avoid the area, reduce speed and drive carefully. Road information may also be available from Main Roads WA by visiting the Main Roads Travel Map, calling 138 138 or by contacting your Local Government Authority.

item.title: Heatwave Advice STAY INFORMED - LOCATIONS BETWEEN ROEBOURNE AND WICKHAM, TO KARRATHA AND DAMPIER.
item.description:
The following alert has been issued by the Department of Health.

Changes to weather outlook.

Time of issue: 02:56 PM

Date of issue: 05 Nov 2026

Heatwave Advice - STAY INFORMED - Locations between Roebourne and Wickham, to Karratha and Dampier.

Higher temperatures are forecast for today (Thursday 5 November) and Friday, with typical temperature conditions returning from Saturday.

WHAT TO DO

People travelling in this area should be prepared for extreme heat.

  • Avoid travelling in the hottest part of the day where possible.

  • Drink water frequently unless your doctor normally limits your fluids.

  • Never leave a person or pet in a vehicle.

  • Avoid exercise and outdoor work in the hottest part of the day.

  • If you must go out, wear a hat and sunscreen and take sufficient water with you.

  • Take shelter in a cool place.

  • If available, use fans or air-conditioners to keep cool.

  • Check in regularly with elderly neighbours and other vulnerable people.

  • Provide shelter and plenty of cool water for pets and other animals.

EXTRA INFORMATION

The Bureau of Meteorology is forecasting a severe heatwave to impact West Pilbara towns today.

Heatwaves are dangerous. Take extra care to prevent heat stress and heat stroke. In extreme circumstances you could be hospitalised or die.

Heatwaves can affect everyone however the following groups are more at risk:

  • Babies and young children

  • Older children and teenagers

  • Pregnant women

  • Older people

  • People with existing physical/mental health conditions or on certain medications

  • People that exercise in the heat

SUPPORT INFORMATION

A heatwave is more than just hot weather. When it is hot during the day and it does not cool down at night, it is hard for your body to cool itself.

If you feel unwell:

  • Call 1800MEDICARE (1800 633 422) for free health advice.

  • See your GP or Health Clinic.

  • For severe or life-threatening symptoms call 000 for an ambulance.

Further support:

  • For more information on heatwaves and how you can plan ahead visit Healthy WA or Aboriginal Health Council of Western Australia.

  • Visit Health Direct How To Handle Heatwave.

  • For information on working in the heat visit Working Safely in Hot Conditions.

  • For the latest heatwave forecast visit Bureau of Meteorology.

  • To receive wellbeing phone calls during heatwaves register for the Australian Red Cross free TeleRedi service or call 1800 188 071.

ACCESSIBILITY

  • Translated heatwave resources are available on the Healthy WA Translated Fact Sheets
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment contact the National Relay Service on 1800 555 677

KEEP UP TO DATE

  • Visit Emergency WA or download the Emergency WA app from the App Store or Google Play.
  • Call 13 DFES (13 3337).
  • Follow DFES on Facebook.
  • Follow HealthyWA or WA Country Health (for regional areas) on Facebook.
  • Listen to ABC Local Radio or news bulletins.

During a power outage, your home phone, computer or other electronic devices connected to the NBN will not work. Include a battery powered radio in your emergency kit.

The next update will be provided tomorrow unless the situation changes.

END

Media Contact: Department of Health Media 9222 4333.
